summary: Intermittent 502/503s traced to KV write-backlog when long-lived streams coincide with large embedding batches
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably Nightingale AI on Dedicated) observed intermittent 502/503 responses over a 6-hour window. Errors cluster when long-lived streaming chat sessions overlap with scheduled bulk embedding uploads. Impact: customer requests return 5xx, elevated error rates for tenant, and degraded p99 latency.

Impact:
- Nightingale reported 15-25% request error rate during peak overlap windows.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embeddings/bulk-upload
- Secondary effects: autoscaler churn on dedicated pool, increased GPU prefetch evictions.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-11 03:35 UTC: Nightingale begins scheduled embedding batch (large batches of 10k vectors) while several streaming sessions remain active for long-lived conversations.
- 2026-03-11 03:43 UTC: Support alerting and metrics show upstream 502/503s spike and kvcache write latencies climbing.
- 2026-03-11 04:10 UTC: Initial mitigation (reduce embedding batch concurrency) applied by CS; errors drop but do not fully resolve.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate 100 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions with keepalive interval 45s.
2) Submit a bulk embedding job (10k items) from the same tenant with 8 concurrent worker uploads.
3) Observe keepalive backlog, kvcache write queue metric spike, followed by API 502/503s.

Observed logs/metrics (examples):
- api-gateway: 502 upstream reset logs correlated with backend write-timeouts.
- serving-runtime: repeated "kvcache_write_backpressure" warning and "prefetch_eviction" entries.
- infra metrics: kvcache_write_queue_depth peaked at 18k, kvcache_write_latency p95 > 2s.
- GPU: brief OOM-suppress events tied to prefetch spillover.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: large embedding batch saturated the kvcache writer pool, and long-lived streams kept sockets/worker slots pinned, amplifying backpressure to api-gateway.
Traces show the api-gateway request to runtime stalls waiting on kvcache write RPCs for >1.5s before upstream reset, causing 502s.
Observed that keepalive sessions are not being recycled quickly on Dedicated nodes; accept-queue shows many "HEARTBEAT" connections in CLOSE_WAIT leading to FD pressure.
SRE reproduced locally by launching streaming load + bulk embedding; tuning embedding concurrency mitigated reproduction severity.
Noted an interaction with TLS session reuse on the dedicated pool; old sessions delaying worker socket reuse increased effective concurrency beyond quota.
Related infra PR (https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2241) contains a diagnostic toggle for kvcache writer pool sizing which was exercised during testing.
comments: 2026-03-11 05:02 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports 20% 5xx over 30m window. Collected request IDs and initial logs; escalated to SRE. Asked customer to pause scheduled embedding as a temporary measure.

2026-03-11 05:55 - SRE (Owen Patel): Confirmed kvcache_write_queue_depth spike. Reproduced with local load test. Proposed short-term: throttle embedding worker concurrency and reduce keepalive window on tenant. Long-term: increase kvcache writer pool and add graceful socket recycling.

2026-03-11 08:12 - Customer (Nightingale Ops): Applied reduced embedding concurrency per Support guidance; errors reduced to 4-6% but still above baseline. Provided extra traces and sample request IDs.

2026-03-12 10:30 - SRE (Owen Patel): Deployed temporary kvcache writer pool bump on dedicated cluster for Nightingale; monitoring shows queue_depth p95 returned to normal and 5xx rate dropped under 1% during a 2-hour window.
2026-03-13 09:45 - Platform Eng (Lena Rivera): Noted TLS keepalive reuse bug on dedicated allocator; adding a socket-reaping patch to next hotfix. Linked INT-4982 for follow-up implementation.
2026-03-13 12:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer acknowledged improvement and requested a post-incident summary and recommended config for embedding jobs.
workaround: Applied: temporarily reduced embedding job concurrency for Nightingale, lowered tenant keepalive window to 15s as a stopgap, and increased kvcache writer pool size on their dedicated cluster. These actions reduced 5xx rate to <1% during monitoring window.
resolution_notes: In progress: permanent fix roadmap includes (1) socket reaping/keepalive fix to avoid FD pinning (linked INT-4982), (2) adaptive kvcache writer autoscaling based on queue_depth, (3) guidance document for customers on safe embedding batch sizes on Dedicated. Postmortem scheduled after full rollback validation.
